page.overview:
What is Dirty Window?

Dirty Window is the fourth song off of American heavy metal band Metallica's eighth studio album St. Anger. It was written by James Hetfield, Lars Ulrich, Kirk Hammett, and Bob Rock.

Like most songs on St. Anger, the subject matter is about alcohol and addiction. Dirty Window specifically is about self-judgment, denial, and putting on a fake front after getting sober. It uses the metaphor of a window that looks clean on the inside but is dirty on the outside, showing how people still remember his past while he thinks of himself as a new person. The lyrics explore feelings of guilt, how one sees themselves, and the constant fight with inner demons, even when they seem to be recovering on the outside. This reflects themes that were often present in Hetfield's personal challenges during that time.

I see my reflection in the window It looks different, so different than what you see Projecting judgment on the world This house is clean baby This house is clean

Am I who I think I am? Am I who I think I am? Am I who I think I am? Look out my window and see it's gone wrong Court is in session and I slam my gavel down
